propositions: Frontier exclusion-list treatment (B) showed higher re-search overlap rates than control (A): 45c1 +78% relative increase, 8d74 +60% relative increase, failing the >=30% reduction requirement on both tickets.

The data-shaped frontier block inserted into the untrusted_ticket_context fence remained inert by design and did not suppress redundant tool calls; in some cases it acted as a signpost, causing the model to immediately re-read files listed under 'already-read' sections.

On the 45c1 ticket, treatment arm passed in attempt 1 (matching control) with higher token cost (+34% output); on 8d74 ticket, treatment required 2 attempts like control but with worse overlap metrics and no cost savings from the frontier.

The cache-seeding mechanism (locust behavior) already removes the dominant redundancy of re-proving credited criteria; remaining re-grounding of unproven criteria cannot be suppressed by a data-shaped exclusion list inside an untrusted fence.

Absolute repeat call counts favored treatment slightly (8d74 B: 8 repeats vs A: 9 repeats; 45c1 B: 4 vs A: 2) but overlap rates penalize efficient runs: 8d74 B2 made only 2 calls with 100% repeat rate, failing to meet the 30% reduction bar required on every ticket.
